source.source_independence: Separate source-parent crosswalk must pass before counting an external study replication

hypothesis: Day-centered same-bird distinct-day altitude distribution shape identity should align across BOTH native GPS and barometric height series on precisely matched GPS events if it is robust to sensor type and not simply a sensor-specific time-constant additive bias.
sensor_caveat: Pressure/barometric height may itself be calibrated using GPS or ambient pressure models; two columns are NOT proven sensor independent without manufacturer metadata. Matched dual height congruence is a robustness diagnostic, not causal identification.
source_selection: Reuse exact previous source-first eligible XY/UTC/speed 5–55m/s/outlier first per bird×UTC day×5min; never replace missing altitude earliest fix with a later fix.
source_population: All 2019-2021 source years, same 28 eligible birds and same frozen 5km cells. Do not select positive height birds afterwards.

vertical_profile.centering: Each native sensor's daily median from identical jointly-complete first-selected flying GPS events in each bird UTC day (across all locations), offline shape, not absolute height prediction
vertical_profile.reference: MEDGULL D1-balanced day and bird equal own-vs-other native GPS log scores; Jeffreys 0.5 each height bin; same target GPS events for both sensors
vertical_profile.note: Original source preheight gate used >=20 events/day; this BEFORE-height dual-sensor analytic endpoint uses the validated existing MEDGULL D1-balanced kernel >=50 evaluation events/day, unlike its >=20 source prescreen. After 50-day admission, if <10 eligible birds, report unavailable; no rescue.
vertical_profile.kernel: Pinned unmodified existing MEDGULL D1-balanced equal bird/day reference kernel: donor minima 1 day-entry, own-other and other-bird other-date events 10, test scored per bird-day >=50; per-bird >=2 scored days.

null.method: 999 whole bird-day identity label permutations within exact UTC date, recompute eligibility for both sensors, do not shuffle native GPS fixes
null.inference: Holm across exactly two sensor outcomes; both supported required for a cross-sensor robustness description on identical fixes.
null.existing_tag_identity_caveat: Same biological animal and tag can remain aliased; two height fields may share calibration error.

descriptive_sensor_diagnostic.metrics: Per bird-day Pearson correlation, robust centered absolute differences (meters), HDOP versus |GPS−baro|; descriptive only, no new quality cutoffs.
descriptive_sensor_diagnostic.missingness: Report source total first-selected 5minute GPS denominator and valid heights separately by sensor and paired.
descriptive_sensor_diagnostic.caution: Mixed pressure-reference height may have varying meteorological offset; no correction after seeing results.

boundary: The question is dual height sensor agreement of individual altitude shape in a new tracking study. Not a Wstar causal effect, not individual-specific wind reaction, and not a taxon-universal law.
no_rescue: No shifting the spatial grain or years, age/source subset, sensor completeness rule, fixed bins, or null comparisons after native height opened.
